Nine Shannon entropy features over raw transaction flow:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eFeature\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eDescription\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF1\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eVolume distribution entropy — detects size clustering\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF2\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCounterparty diversity entropy — detects address concentration\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF3\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eTemporal spacing entropy — detects timing anomalies\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF4\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eContract interaction entropy — detects single-target focus\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF5\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eGas usage entropy — detects pattern rigidity\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF6\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eToken flow concentration entropy — detects unidirectional flows\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF7\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCross-chain activity spread — detects chain-specific hiding\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF8\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eValue magnitude distribution — detects logarithmic attack stacking\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eF9\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eMEV interaction frequency — detects sandwich and frontrun patterns\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWeights are learned by FAISS (Phase 2 learning) at every 1,000-vector depth milestone. Observer-effect correction:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"M(t)     = 1 − PI_t / PI_baseline      (L3.1 — prediction interval narrowing)\nOE_factor = corr(signal_pub(t−1), behavioral_change(t))   (L3.2)\nM_adj(t) = M_base(t) × (1 − OE_factor)\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eM(t)     = 1 − PI_t / PI_baseline      (L3.1 — prediction interval narrowing)\nOE_factor = corr(signal_pub(t−1), behavioral_change(t))   (L3.2)\nM_adj(t) = M_base(t) × (1 − OE_factor)\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen an entity's behavior changes \u003cem\u003eafter\u003c/em\u003e a TRION signal is published about it, the mental score degrades. <p dir="auto"><strong>Multi-Chain Behavioral Truth Oracle — Pre-Execution DeFi Firewall</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">TRION derives cryptographically verified behavioral signals from the complete on-chain record of every entity across <strong>100 chains and 13 VM families</strong>. It answers one question before any trade executes: <em>is this wallet acting like an attacker right now?</em> Any DeFi protocol, AI agent, or execution layer calls <code>TRIONExecutionGate.checkExecution(address)</code> to block hostile wallets before damage occurs — not after.</p>
<p dir="auto">This is not a price oracle. It is a behavioral intelligence layer operating at the intersection of information theory, cryptography, and decentralized consensus. It would have blocked <strong>$44B+</strong> in historical DeFi exploits.</p>

<p dir="auto">The 64 behavioral archetypes are trained by K-means against the accumulated FAISS index. Each archetype maps to a canonical behavioral identity with a risk classification:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Archetypes include:</strong> Hero, Jester, Sage, Shadow, Innocent, Rebel, Caregiver, Creator — mapped against risk levels from <code>SAFE</code> through <code>CRITICAL</code>. Attack archetypes (<code>MEV_BOT</code>, <code>ORACLE_ATTACKER</code>, <code>FLASH_BORROWER</code>, <code>GOVERNANCE_CAPTURER</code>, <code>WASH_TRADER</code>, <code>BRIDGE_DRAINER</code>) are trained on historical exploit address vectors.</p>
<p dir="auto">Archetype assignment: <code>k-NN(entity_vector, centroids)</code> → nearest centroid by cosine similarity.</p>

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre class="notranslate"><code>DeFi Protocol calls: checkExecution(entityId, caller)

1. Retrieve latest BehavioralSignal for entityId from on-chain storage
2. Unpack uint256: status(8) ‖ phi_t(32) ‖ theta(32) ‖ dropPct(16) ‖ ...
3. Evaluate gating condition:
     STATUS_SAFE     (1) → allowed = true
     STATUS_ELEVATED (2) → allowed = true  (warn only)
     STATUS_COLLAPSE (3) → allowed = false  ← BLOCKED
     STATUS_HOSTILE  (4) → allowed = false  ← BLOCKED + alert event
4. Compute: decisionHash = keccak256(entityId, caller, status, block.number)
5. Store: ExecutionDecision { allowed, decisionHash, timestamp } in mapping
6. Increment: totalExecutionsAllowed or totalExecutionsBlocked
7. Return: (bool allowed, bytes32 decisionHash)

<p dir="auto">The BTV engine (<code>oracle_api/price_feed_routes.py</code>, 532 lines) implements TRION's "Truth Hierarchy" — an alternative price that accounts for behavioral evidence:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre class="notranslate"><code>BTV(asset, t) = CEX_price(asset, t) × (1 − MF(entity, t))
